h1: Network Hero — Agencies & Studios Hero Section Design
tagline: “Unlock Top Marketing Talent You Thought Was Out of Reach -- Now Just One Click Away!” — the whole hero section is composed around that line, down to the animation timings.
summary: Hero section reference for an agency or studio — 35ms transitions, #070319 base, a 640x472 frame and React and Vite.
about: Network Hero solves the hero section problem for an agency or studio with a single captured brief. “Unlock Top Marketing Talent You Thought Was Out of Reach -- Now Just One Click Away!” is the line the layout is built to carry. The palette is deep indigo #070319 underneath, white #FFFFFF for the type and indigo #A068FF carrying the accents, set in Inter. The reference is built with React and Vite, and the layout decisions are stated independently of it. Motion is 35ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), kept quiet enough that the copy still leads. Keep it open while you write: the 7,543-character brief is the part that transfers to your own page.

layout.title: Navigation held to one row
layout.body: Wordmark, links and the #A068FF action share one baseline, which is what keeps a thin row from looking accidental. The links are set below the wordmark in size, and the #A068FF action is the only element in the bar with any weight. Give the wordmark no more room than its type needs.

layout.title: Sizes fixed in the brief
layout.body: Sizes were read off the render at 640x472: 64px spacing steps, 35ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) easing. There is no invented intermediate value between the named ones; the measurement list is the whole system.

layout.title: Top row: wordmark, links, one action
layout.body: Test the bar over your own media before giving it a background. The reference was captured at 640x472.

layout.title: Values you can check
layout.body: Spacing is quoted the same way (64px spacing steps, 35ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) easing), not as a scale that grows on its own.

motion.title: Short, named durations
motion.body: Motion in the controls is short and repeatable: 35ms on each state change. The values are short enough to read as feedback rather than as animation.

motion.title: One element arrives
motion.body: Entrance motion is spent on the page's own message rather than on the frame around it: a typewriter pass types the intro line. The entrance is confined to the elements it names, so the rest of the layout never animates.

fonts.name: Inter
fonts.weights: Weight not fixed in the brief
fonts.role: Headline and interface text — one face for the whole page

notes: Transitions are specified at 35ms, short enough that the page never feels like it is waiting for an animation.

Accent and ground are both named (indigo #A068FF on deep indigo #070319), so a brand swap moves one value.

customize: Retune #A068FF for your brand only after the Inter copy is final, and re-check the contrast on the darkest band.
Swap in your own headline where “Unlock Top Marketing Talent You Thought Was Out of Reach -- Now Just One Click Away!” sits and keep the line breaks, because the entrance animates per line.
Replace #A068FF last, after the copy is final, and test it against #070319 at the smallest text size on the page.
Swap #A068FF for your brand colour and re-check it against #070319, since the accent is the only place saturation is allowed.

editorial.title: Making the hero section yours
editorial.body: Change the content first and check the frame afterwards. 64px spacing steps, 35ms transitions and cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) easing are the values to protect while you swap the copy. The subject is the part that should change.

editorial.title: The timing behind the hero section
editorial.body: Every transition here has a number attached. That is why 35ms transitions, a typewriter pass and per-character headline timing can be ported value by value instead of re-tuned by feel. Nothing animates for its own sake in this hero section.

editorial.title: What an agency or studio gains here
editorial.body: The design argues its case on one screen. The media is a still at 640x472. The media carries the atmosphere, the copy carries the offer, and 64px spacing steps and 35ms transitions keep the two apart. It gives a agency reader the shortest honest route to the offer.

faq.question: What does the brief behind Network Hero actually contain?
faq.answer: The captured brief runs 7,543 characters and covers the frame, the type scale, the palette and the transitions. Copying it gives you that text, and sending it to Studio stages the same request with the page already described.

faq.question: Do I need React and Vite to rebuild Network Hero?
faq.answer: No. The brief is a specification, not a dependency list. It was written for React and Vite, but the same composition rebuilds in whatever you already use. The stack is named so you know how the reference was made.

faq.question: How do the 35ms transitions in Network Hero behave?
faq.answer: Entrances and state changes are in the 35ms range on cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1). They are driven by state changes rather than a scroll library, and they never hold up the copy.

audience: Anyone using an AI builder who wants a brief that already contains a 640x472 frame instead of leaving it to the model.
